text: With p of a program parallelisable, the best speedup on n processors is 1/((1-p) + p/n). At p = 0.95, what is the ceiling?
choices: Twenty, no matter how many processors you buy — and about thirteen on 24 cores.
There is no ceiling; the speedup grows without bound as n increases.
Ninety-five percent of n, so about 23 on 24 cores.
About 1.05, since only the parallel fraction benefits.
explanation: The sequential part dominates, and at p = 0.5 the ceiling is 2. That is why the practical rule is to find out what fraction of the time is actually in the part you can divide before parallelising anything — Chapter 18's insistence on measuring first, with extra force here, because concurrency also costs correctness and paying that for a 1.3-times speedup is a bad trade.
